profile.aboutVerbatim:
Hello! I am Md. Nafizur Rahman, a dedicated Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) student at the Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, University of Rajshahi, Bangladesh. My academic journey is built upon a strong foundation in Anatomy, Histology, Physiology, Pathology, Parasitology, Microbiology, Medicine, Surgery, Epidemiology, and Public Health. I am deeply passionate about bridging the gap between biological research and advanced computational science to improve animal welfare, public health, and disease prevention.

Throughout my journey, I have integrated traditional veterinary science with modern Data Analytics, developing proficiency in Python, SQL, and data visualization tools like GeoPandas and Matplotlib to drive evidence-based research.

My core research vision unites clinical surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, molecular parasitology, and next-generation nanomedicine under the unified One Health framework. Beyond academia, I actively serve in wildlife rescue operations with SWAN Bangladesh and volunteer clinical veterinary care for campus and stray animals.
profile.technicalSideBio: Beyond the lab coat, I'm a self-driven developer who ships real products through "Vibe Coding" — an AI-assisted, rapid-prototyping workflow where a clear idea turns into a working app in days, not months. I work primarily with Python, SQL, and the web stack (HTML · CSS · JavaScript), pairing clean backend logic with modern, responsive interfaces.

researchProjects.title: Ectoparasites in Free-Roaming Dogs from the Semi-Arid Barind Tract
researchProjects.subtitle: Epidemiology, species distribution, morphological identification, and molecular characterization
researchProjects.overview: This comprehensive one-year study investigated the ectoparasitic burden on 310 free-roaming dogs in Bangladesh's semi-arid Barind Tract. By combining field surveillance with advanced morphological and molecular analyses, the project identified novel parasite species in the region, highlighting critical One Health implications regarding zoonotic disease risks and animal welfare.
researchProjects.methodology: A rigorous year-long cross-sectional survey (Nov 2024 – Dec 2025). Physically collected 2,908 ectoparasites across 310 dogs using systematic combing and fine forceps. Laboratory examination utilized taxonomic keys, oculometers for morphometric measurements, and advanced molecular characterization (COX1 and 18S rRNA sequencing) to confirm tick species. Applied negative binomial and multivariable logistic regression models in R to assess environmental and demographic risk factors.
keyArtefacts: Documented 2,908 ectoparasites including fleas, lice, and ticks.
First morphological record of Ctenocephalides orientis and Heterodoxus spiniger in Bangladesh.
Identified genetic mutation maps at COX1 site 370 for Haemaphysalis bispinosa.
Established risk factor models showing adult age and poor body condition scores significantly elevate infestation intensity.
researchProjects.collaborations: Worked with a multidisciplinary team coordinating field assistants for safe handling/restraint of free-roaming dogs, laboratory technicians for Sanger sequencing of tick vectors, and faculty co-researchers for taxonomic and statistical validation.
researchProjects.outcomes: Established foundational baseline data and critical epidemiological evidence underscoring the urgent necessity of integrated veterinary, environmental, and public health interventions in Bangladesh's semi-arid ecosystems.

researchProjects.title: Clinical Surveillance and Antimicrobial Stewardship in Companion Animals
researchProjects.subtitle: Evaluating Veterinary Prescribing Patterns, Owner KAP, and Self-Medication Behaviors in Rajshahi, Bangladesh (A One Health Perspective)
researchProjects.overview: This 12-month prospective clinical surveillance investigates antimicrobial prescribing patterns, disease prevalence, owner KAP (Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices), and self-medication behaviors in companion animals across private veterinary practices in Rajshahi, Bangladesh. Driven by rapid ongoing data collection to build a comprehensive dataset well beyond the initial 385-case baseline, the study aims to establish the region's first One Health database.
researchProjects.objectives: (i) Determine proportional prevalence, seasonal patterns, and demographic correlates of companion animal clinical syndromes; (ii) Evaluate veterinary antimicrobial prescribing habits and empirical stewardship gaps; (iii) Assess pet owner KAP, biosecurity practices, and unauthorized home self-medication behaviors.
researchProjects.summary: Companion animals play an integral role in urban households but serve as potential reservoirs for zoonotic pathogens and antimicrobial-resistant bacteria under the One Health framework. Irrational antibiotic usage, combined with OTC self-medication by pet owners, poses alarming risks of treatment failure and fatal pet toxicosis. This project provides empirical evidence to formulate rational prescribing guidelines.
researchProjects.outcomes: Developing the first regional clinical database, establishing antimicrobial resistance surveillance benchmarks, and providing evidence for targeted public health campaigns and regulatory enforcement.

researchProjects.title: Species Distribution and Risk Factors of Bedbug (Cimex spp.) Infestation in Student Residences
researchProjects.subtitle: Cross-sectional entomological and epidemiological survey at the University of Rajshahi
researchProjects.overview: This cross-sectional survey investigates the prevalence, species distribution, and risk factors of bedbug (Cimex spp.) infestations in high-density student hostels at the University of Rajshahi, Bangladesh. By analyzing environmental variables and conducting morphological identification across a random sample of 370 beds, the study evaluates infestation loads and associated sleep disturbances.
researchProjects.objectives: (i) Determine the prevalence and intensity of bedbug infestation among hostel residents; (ii) Identify the distribution of bedbug species (Cimex lectularius vs. Cimex hemipterus); (iii) Assess environmental and behavioral risk factors linked to infestation.
researchProjects.methodology: Randomized sampling of 370 beds calculated with a 95% confidence interval and 5% margin of error across 10,000 university beds. Collected specimens preserved in 96% ethanol and examined under stereomicroscopes and 200x optical lenses. Multi-variable logistic regression analyzes factors such as room occupancy, bed-frame material, floor level, used furniture history, and sleep disturbance indices.
researchProjects.outcomes: Provides critical baseline epidemiological data to guide hostel administration health management, optimize targeted non-chemical and chemical vector control, and improve student living standards.

researchProjects.title: Socio-Veterinary Determinants of Pet Healthcare Behavior in Bangladesh
researchProjects.subtitle: A Comprehensive Statistical Study of Pet Ownership Patterns and Welfare Challenges
researchProjects.overview: This research investigates the socio-veterinary factors influencing pet healthcare behaviors, preventive practices, and barriers to veterinary access across seven administrative divisions of Bangladesh. By analyzing demographic variables and owner challenges, the study highlights the critical role of education in improving pet welfare.
researchProjects.objectives: Investigate socio-demographic determinants shaping pet ownership across Bangladesh, evaluate the influence of educational attainment on preventive vaccination and veterinary visit frequencies, and identify structural barriers to healthcare accessibility.
researchProjects.methodology: Cross-sectional survey of 361 pet-owning households across Bangladesh. Employs Chi-square tests of independence, Spearman rank correlation, and multi-nominal logistic regression in SPSS and R.
researchProjects.outcomes: Revealed strong statistically significant associations (p < 0.001) between owner educational level and vaccination adherence as well as veterinary clinic visitation frequency. Formed the foundation for an accepted paper in the Journal of Advanced Veterinary and Animal Research (JAVAR).

researchProjects.title: Morphological and Molecular Detection of Capillaria spp. in Native Poultry
researchProjects.subtitle: Investigating nematode parasitism in native chicken and ducks of Northern Bangladesh
researchProjects.overview: Assisting in sample collection, post-mortem intestinal scraping, morphological identification, and molecular characterization of Capillaria species infecting indigenous backyard chickens and ducks in northern rural communities.
researchProjects.methodology: Gastrointestinal tract necropsy, microscopic identification of characteristic bipolar plugged Capillaria ova and spicules, formalin-ether sedimentation, and PCR amplification of ribosomal DNA targets.
researchProjects.outcomes: Characterizing species diversity of helminths affecting indigenous poultry production, helping formulate cost-effective anthelmintic deworming protocols for rural subsistence farmers.

researchProjects.title: Vector-Borne & Infectious Disease Surveillance (Arboviruses)
researchProjects.subtitle: Entomo-virological monitoring of Dengue, Chikungunya, and Japanese Encephalitis in local mosquito vectors
researchProjects.overview: Conducting proactive entomo-virological monitoring to detect Dengue, Chikungunya, and Japanese Encephalitis viruses in local mosquito populations. Integrates vector infectivity rates with spatial GIS and meteorological variables to generate the region's first proactive early-warning surveillance framework.
researchProjects.methodology: Trapping adult mosquitoes using BG Sentinel traps, CDC light traps, and larval dipping across high-risk urban and peri-urban hubs. Laboratory homogenization, viral RNA extraction, RT-PCR pathogen detection, and calculation of Minimum Infection Rates (MIR).
researchProjects.outcomes: Generated the region's first entomo-virological baseline data, unmasked co-circulation dynamics of Dengue and Chikungunya, and developed a functional predictive early-warning framework for local health authorities.

researchProjects.title: Nanoparticle-Based Rabies Vaccines in Mice: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
researchProjects.subtitle: Comparative Immunogenicity, Protective Efficacy, and Safety (PRISMA Protocol Registered on OSF)
researchProjects.overview: Rabies remains a fatal zoonotic disease with near 100% lethality. Traditional inactivated vaccines require strict cold chains and multi-dose regimens that challenge low-resource nations. This study systematically synthesizes preclinical in vivo data on advanced nanovaccines (mRNA-LNPs, VLPs, nano-adjuvants, and polymeric carriers) to evaluate their potential for single-dose protection.
researchProjects.methodology: Registered PRISMA-P protocol on the Open Science Framework. Systematic multi-database literature search across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase. Quantitative meta-analysis using Random-Effects models in R (meta / metafor packages) analyzing Virus-Neutralizing Antibody (VNA) titers across Days 5, 7, 14, 21, and 28, post-challenge survival rates, and safety biodistribution.
researchProjects.outcomes: Establishes a quantitative evidence base accelerating the clinical translation of single-dose nanotherapeutics for human and veterinary rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

researchProjects.title: PoultryMedix: Autonomous Multimodal AI for Avian Health & AMR Stewardship
researchProjects.subtitle: AI-driven triage, RAG veterinary pharmacopeia, and automated prescription withdrawal period surveillance
researchProjects.context: Developed under the AI Battle, AI Navigator Programme (Send a little Hope UK)
researchProjects.overview: PoultryMedix is an AI-driven veterinary diagnostic and epidemiological platform designed for marginal poultry farmers in Bangladesh. Rooted in the One Health framework, it utilizes multi-modal AI to diagnose avian diseases and actively combats Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) by enforcing drug withdrawal periods through automated prescription scanning.
features: Omni-Modal AI Diagnostics: Multi-layered triage synthesizing lesion/fecal visual imagery, acoustic respiratory distress recordings, and rural voice symptoms.

AMR Shield via OCR & RAG: Built-in Optical Character Recognition scans handwritten vet prescriptions and cross-references a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation knowledge base (built from national veterinary pharmacopeia & WHO AMR guidelines) to issue automated alerts on drug withdrawal periods.
GPS Outbreak Surveillance: Every logged case generates geolocation coordinates to plot real-time outbreak heatmaps for local Upazila Livestock Offices and the Department of Livestock Services (DLS).
Ethical AI Governance: Operates as a 'Thinking Partner' triaging mild issues and escalating complex emergencies directly to registered veterinarians.

conferencePapers.title: Navigating Pet Welfare in Bangladesh: A Multilayered Analysis of Ownership, Ethics and Service Accessibility
conferencePapers.conference: 1st Scientific Conference on Innovation, Application and Future Trends in Animal Health and Production
conferencePapers.organizer: Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, University of Rajshahi, Rajshahi-6205, Bangladesh
conferencePapers.abstract: Pet ownership in Bangladesh is experiencing a gradual transformation, shaped by evolving social, cultural, and economic dynamics. There is no study on the intersection of demographic trends, ethical considerations, and structural challenges in ensuring pet welfare in Bangladesh. This research aims to describe the socio-demographic profiles of pet ownership in Bangladesh and to investigate the impact of age, gender, and education on pet ownership. A mixed-method approach was used with a cross-sectional survey of 361 households across the country. The data were collected through a survey questionnaire and face-to-face interviews. Chi-square tests of independence examined associations between education, gender, and specific pet ownership categories, while Spearman correlation was used to analyze the relationship between age and the total number of pets they owned. The results revealed nearly equal engagement with pets (52.9% male, 47.1% female), with the largest share of respondents aged 18-25 years (52.6%). Cats were the most frequently owned pets (56.2%), followed by birds (35.5%), dogs (11.1%), rabbits (5.0%), and others (3.9%). Education level significantly influenced cat (x² = 32.180, p < .001) and bird ownership (x² = 27.010, p < .001), while no such associations were found for dogs, rabbits, or other pets. Public opinion strongly favored government involvement in pet welfare (88.9%), though support varied significantly across divisions (x² = 27.775, p = 0.006), being highest in Barisal and Rangpur and lower in Dhaka and Rajshahi. The findings provide valuable information for policymakers, veterinary services, and animal welfare organizations to promote sustainable and humane pet welfare in Bangladesh.

conferencePapers.title: Challenges and Opportunities in Veterinary Care, Feed, and Maintenance of Pets in Bangladesh
conferencePapers.conference: International Conference on Transdisciplinary Integration of Terrestrial and Aquatic Ecosystems for Advancing Health, Food Security, and Nutrition
conferencePapers.organizer: Chattogram Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (CVASU), Khulshi, Chattogram-4225, Bangladesh
conferencePapers.abstract: Pet ownership is thriving in Bangladesh, but most owners are not aware of the challenges and benefits of pet care. As a result, they encounter several problems during rearing. Therefore, sustainable pet keeping and care remain limited in Bangladesh. This study aims to investigate pet feeding practices, veterinary access, and common problems faced by owners. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 361 pet owners using a structured questionnaire. A random sampling technique was used in the data collection. Data were analyzed by SPSS to observe the correlation among different variables. The results indicated that the majority of participants owned one pet (38.0%), followed by two pets (19.1%), and three to five pets (15.0%). Interestingly, a substantial portion of respondents indicated that they owned more than five pets (n = 101, 28.0%). The results indicated a significant difference (P < 0.001) in monthly food costs among the fully vaccinated, partially vaccinated, and unvaccinated groups. The results showed a significant relationship between education level and vaccination status (P < 0.001). Furthermore, the findings revealed a significant association between education level and frequency of veterinary visits (P < 0.001). It was noticed that higher education is strongly associated with proactive animal healthcare practices, whereas lower education correlates with reduced use of veterinary services.

fieldworkWildlife.title: Wildlife Rescue & Rehabilitation — SWAN Bangladesh
fieldworkWildlife.description: "Wildlife conservation is not just about saving animals; it is about preserving the delicate ecological balance that sustains us all. As a veterinary student and a trained member of Save Wildlife and Nature (SWAN), Bangladesh, I am deeply committed to the ethical rescue, rehabilitation, and safe relocation of urban and rural wildlife. My fieldwork primarily focuses on mitigating human-animal conflicts through community awareness and hands-on rescue operations, including the safe capture and relocation of snakes and other local fauna. Through a 'One Health' approach, I strive to ensure the well-being of both the animals and the communities they interact with."

hobbies.title: Smartphone Photography
hobbies.description: In my free time, photography is my favorite way to unwind and express my creativity. Using just my smartphone, I love capturing the best moments of life and the everyday beauty of nature. I believe you don't need expensive gear to take a great photo—it's all about the perspective. Whether it's a striking natural landscape or a simple daily scene, I always strive to bring a clean, professional touch to my shots, turning fleeting moments into lasting memories.

For me, cooking is a therapeutic and rewarding process that brings joy and relaxation to everyday life.
